logic_gh_9gates.gif: Replay of ui/static/logic_examples/greenberg_hastings.logic.json (9 gates) from a sparse random start (the D2.5 regime; seed 1). Yellow = excited, blue = refractory. A learned 1,598-gate circuit simplified against its own dynamics; it equals the KNOWN generating rule on all 262,144 neighbourhoods. Recovery of a synthetic rule, not a rule discovered from Bad Apple.
logic_realvideo_failure.gif: Replay of ui/static/logic_examples/d4_G_s0_b144k.logic.json from frame 3996 with its 2-frame observation prefix, then free. The circuit holds the silhouette for a few steps, then turns it into a growing blob (docs/path-d/D4_LOG.md). Left: derived 48x36 frames of Bad Apple!!.
nca_state.gif: Numpy replay of runs/featured/whole_song_s0.ncab from frame 0 (no frames injected), shown for frames 1850-1939: the thresholded visible channel and 3 of the 15 hidden channels (each min-max scaled over the clip). The rule in effect changes at phase boundaries (external schedule).
nca_vs_original.gif: Frames 1850-2029 (every 2nd), original 48x36 binary frame vs. the featured export's numpy replay from frame 0. The NCA uses 110 phase rules on an external schedule plus carried hidden state; it reproduces this one video (4.2 MB model), it is not a general video generator.
shape_ring.gif: runs/shape/synth_preds.npz. All three are hand-written rules driven by ORACLE controls chosen from the intended frames. The lattice transport (9 control nodes, smooth interpolated field; the interpolation is non-local) keeps the ring connected; region-wise shifts tear it.
